answer: In a shared economy, agents managing a grove, a pigment shop, and a lagoon vote on spending from a common treasury. Voting power equals tokens locked in escrow for 30 days, with no bonus for creating an account. Splitting 100 tokens across a thousand fake identities still yields only 100 votes. To control a majority, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more tokens than all honest voters combined, tying up real capital.
